name: S. S.
quote: This pan is miraculous. Follow me here... After learning the truth about "ceramic" nonstick electric skillets, I could no longer use them... it's actually some kind of liquid chemicals mixed with ceramic that wears off overtime, which means it wears off onto/into the food that you cook and eat. I have always made my cassava flour tortillas and flat bread on "ceramic" electric skillets and these are a staple to me, so I tried to find an alternative and I tried a 100% pure ceramic pan which seemed like an absolute joke (it was the worst pan I ever tried and could not cook it only burnt and unevenly no less and took forever to do so, and it stuck horribly, I don't even understand how they sell them to be honest)... so the pure ceramic was a fail, and I didn't really want to do cast-iron because it takes time to break it in and I don't really fry anything so I don't see how I would end up seasoning it and it just seemed like a lot of work and a lot of trying plus I honestly don't like how eventually the stuff on cast-iron wears off too, and you have to make sure you know what the company used on it to season it, plus apparently if you like over fry stuff in it, it can produce trans fats because of something that happens with the iron, I don't know, just too much to worry about. So I thought that I might just have to forgo one of my favorite recipes. But I decided to try siiraats nonstick titanium pan, and I honestly did not expect it to go well, but it went miraculously well! It behaved like something unnatural that makes things work really easy, except it's completely safe and natural. My tortillas and bread came out perfect. It was so easy to cook on. It did not stick at all, and this is really doughy gluten-free flour we're talking about, and I make huge ones so I have the large pan and it uses up the whole pan. I don't like to use a lot of oil so there's only the oil that's in the dough and then that tiny bit of oil that you drop onto the pan which I found spread really easily. The oil doesn't smoke (so far I've used unrefined, cold-pressed avocado oil), the pan heats up really evenly, and it just cooks so well, it is amazing. My bread came out the best it ever has and it does so every time (I made the recipe on this pan so far about eight times). It's even better than my nonstick ceramic electric skillets that I used to use for years. It's an absolute joy to cook on and it's easy to clean and it's very forgiving. I found that when I thought I ruined my bread by having it initially land too far to the side and be sort of bent up against the side I thought that it would just like not work and part of it would break off, but it actually cooked it well and thoroughly so I could flip it in one piece and it came out amazingly. When I left one on a little too long and it started to darken, it did not get burning on the pan and there was no smoke and it was just very forgiving. This is the best pan I've ever used and I honestly don't see a reason to buy another pan in the future. I also got their titanium spatula and it is a huge help to be able to use a metal spatula on a pan. You have to be careful with the ceramic ones and nonstick because everything can scratch and everything does scratch, but the titanium spatula is nice and flat so you can really just flip things better particularly tortillas and flatbread and things that you want something very thin to slide under. There's no creepy materials in any of the stuff and it's just great. No weird chemical smells nothing. It's all just amazing. What's so incredible about it is that it is completely nontoxic and completely natural and yet it cooks like something that is made for convenience, which usually means toxic materials, so the point is is that this pan accomplished doing things in the right way while also cooking just as conveniently as all that toxic crap promises and allows; it is the best of both worlds and a game changer thusly. But again, in my experience, this works so much better than nonstick pans. My stuff used to stick to Teflon all the time when I used to use that but the electric skillet even had sticking issues and also burning issues. This just works so much better. And besides just working, it must just cook through better due to how it distributes heat because my torillas and flatbread (depending on how thin or thick you make them but same recipe) really just come out absolutely perfect with no doughy spots and no burnt spots and they just seem more evenly cooked. It just seems to cook more uniform for me, like very noticeably so. This pan allowed me to perfect my recipe and make it so much easier at the same time.

name: Terry C.
quote: It all started with a late night impulse purchase (we all know about those!) which I almost immediately regretted for mainly financial reasons (having later seen the same or what looked like the same items online for a lower price). I contacted the company within an hour to try to cancel for a full refund. I received a reply almost instantly but was told it was already too late, the order already was in fulfillment mode. If I wanted to get a refund, I would have to await the delivery of the items and then go through the return process. This obviously put me in a very disgruntled mood. However, I was offered a further discount on the cookware but I had already made up my mind to obtain a refund. I do not blame the company for this reasonable counter offer but made me even more determined that the product was overpriced and not needed. I completely take responsibility for my mistake in ordering and accept the inconvenience that was to come but I must admit that I initially felt that the company could have been more accommodating in canceling the order. However, it is the customer service experience which really became the focus of this whole debacle. My agent was pleasant, courteous, patient, responsive from the start, despite my own impatience and frustration which I am sure was evident in my communication. All emails were attended to quickly and each thread moved me closer to the goal of a full refund, but it did take some effort and time, about 3 weeks in total. Of course, it was my own fault for placing the order in the first place and I was more frustrated with myself for having made a wrong decision. At some point I realised that I was communicating to an AI assisted channel simply because of the consistency of the measured and supportive replies but that no longer mattered because at least I was getting the exact support I needed to complete the refund process which in due course was resolved with a full refund (minus a postal return fee which was reasonable due to the fact it was a change of mind return). I cannot comment on the quality of the product as I returned the parcels unopened, but I can commend the customer service most highly in my particular situation. I know the reviews of the product and customer service have been mixed but in my experience, the company in good faith did follow through with their refund policy and I've never had more personable communication throughout the process. Best of luck to anyone reading this for making the right decision for your cookware and hope you will receive the same level of service and satisfying resolution if ever needed.

name: Jeremy
quote: Ordered very expensive titanium pans in late May, received in a timely manner. I have worked in professional kitchens in France and cooked with countless pans over the years. I cooked a basic egg and cheese, and ended up with a burnt, welded-on mess that required serious effort to clean. Not exactly the "effortless release" you'd expect from a premium pan at this price point. I gave it another shot with specific instructions via email from the company: asparagus in avocado oil, which started out reasonably well — until I added fresh garlic. On the same medium heat setting, it burnt immediately. The pan cannot handle even simple aromatics without scorching. I have emailed probably 50 times back and forth, giving photos. I ordered three pans, washed one in the dishwasher and never used it. The third is in the original packaging and never opened. They refused to return my money, wanted to give me a percentage off and pay $20 for return shipping. They offer a "100 day trial, hassle free guarantee". Well, it has been full of hassle and they won't accept a return without major loss for a product that simply doesn't work.

name: Erin O.

name: Michael B.
quote: Buyers should be aware that once you use your new SiraatsKitchen pan... YOU OWN IT. There is no return. The company's Refund Policy is unrealistic and frankly, the way it is worded on the company's website it is unethical. The Return Policy starts with: "We're confident you'll love cooking with Siraat. That's why every order comes with a 100-day trial period, from the day it arrives at your door. Use it, cook with it, and see the difference for yourself. If it's not for you, we'll take it back. No complicated process." Customers need to scroll down the page before realizing what that really means. I had to find out the hard way. In the Return Policy section with the heading "Used Products" the first sentence reads "We encourage you to actually cook with your Siraat, that's the whole point of the trial. If you've been using the product and feel it's not performing as expected, reach out to our team." Here's what happened to me: I reached out to customer support to request a refund as I was not happy with the product's performance. The Siraat support team requested detailed explanations and photos which I supplied. It wasn't until the fourth frustrating email exchanges that customer support explained that company policy states that once the product has been used, it cannot be returned. The 100-day trial means that for up to 100 days you can drive yourself crazy with ridiculous email exchanges with Siraat customer support trying to explain to you how to use a frying pan. My pan now sits in a drawer. Not because I can't get it to work... I don't want to make the effort, and I don't want to do business with a company that misleads their customers. I brought this to the attention of the company so they can at the very least restate their policies, but they have not done so. Not for nothin' but with all the high-end nonstick pans out there today, I strongly urge buying one that has a reasonable return policy such as Hex Clad or Made In. 6/16/2026 Update: Immediately after my original review was published, SiraatsKitchen Customer Support once again contacted me. The company offered to resolve this issue satisfactorily. I will say that SiraatsKitchen Customer Support pays attention and responds quickly.

The "naturally non-stick performance" claim is also questionable; titanium is not inherently non-stick. For these reasons I chose to cancel the order. Look at all the 4 and 5 star one line reviews! Those don't look genuine! Most frustratingly, the website prominently advertises free returns, yet when I initiated a return I had to pay $14.95 USD. That directly contradicts the 'FREE RETURNS' displayed at the top of the site. I had to provide photos of the pan and lid as part of the return, even though I've not opened the package and assuming I eventually get a refund, that's going to take another 5-10 business days. This experience has cost me time, money, and effort. I will not be buying from this company again. UPDATE: I did receive a full refund, which included the return postage cost, which I am grateful for.

quote: I rarely leave negative reviews, but this process became far more difficult and stressful than it needed to be. I purchased several pans from Siraat Kitchen based on the heavy marketing around their "non-stick" performance and "100-day trial / hassle-free guarantee." Unfortunately, my experience did not reflect those claims. After carefully following their instructions, including the preheating and water test, food still stuck to the pan during the very first use. That was disappointing considering the premium price point. If you are specifically looking for genuinely non-stick pans, these are not. I also had concerns regarding the condition of some items upon arrival, as there were visible marks that made the products appear less than brand new. What became most frustrating, however, was the returns and refund process. Communication was extremely repetitive and drawn out. I was asked multiple times for the same photos and information, even after: - sending images repeatedly - receiving return approval - being issued a return label - returning the items - and the company confirming receipt of the returned goods At one stage, I was even asked again for photos of items that were already physically back in their possession. The process did eventually end with a refund being issued, but only after persistent follow-up over an extended period. For a company advertising a "hassle-free guarantee," the experience was anything but hassle-free. To be fair, the company did eventually respond and process the refund, which is why I am not leaving a 1-star review. However, the overall experience left me disappointed, particularly given the price of the products and the amount of effort required to resolve the issue. I allowed the skillet to cool and I was able to rinse without soap, using only a soft towel and warm water to clean. The best part is I no longer have to worry about harmful toxins. I am so impressed with my purchase that I have shared my experience with others to experience and join the SiraatsKitchen family of satisfied purchasers.

name: Matthew F.
quote: This company is apparently a complete scam-- and I'm sorry I didn't read the reviews on Trustpilot before I purchased this pan. Food sticks, instantly. I tried several times, having watched all the videos, done the "water test," the "shimmering oil," etc. Nothing worked. The pan is cheaply designed and not at all nonstick. Totally false advertising. Also false? The return policy. The website states that they have a 100 day trial period-- "use it, cook with it, see the difference for yourself. If it's not for you, we'll take it back. No complicated process." WELL, that's not true. they refused my return after requesting photos. The pan is spotless (I only used it four times on an induction stovetop). Not only is it a complicated return process, but apparently they don't offer this trial period at all. It's just a slick internet company selling trash-worthy pans at inflated prices. I fell for it. I initiated a charge-back on my credit card. We'll see what happens. Definitely will check trustpilot in the future. -- by the way-- if customer service responds below-- THEY ARE LYING. The customer service is a runaround. As you can see from reading other reviews from people who have had a similar experience, there is no resolution available. UPDATE: After I published this review, I continued to correspond with the company to try to return the pan. There were something like twenty emails back and forth, in which the company shamefully and flagrantly misrepresented their return policy (the "trial period" is actually, to them, a period of "coaching and email support," and not a meaningful "trial" in which one of the outcomes can be that you return the item because it failed the trial). Before the chargeback process was complete, the company saw my trustpilot review and gave me a complete refund. They have emailed me twice now to ask that I update my review to reflect the "final outcome." Here's the update. I would encourage the company to actually change the return policy page on their website to make it clear that they don't accept returns of used items, and that the 100 day trial period doesn't exist in any meaningful, plain-language way. They are selling a product at a high comparative price. I encourage Siraat to be a more responsible and professional company. Stand by your plain language terms. If you say stand by your product, stand by your trial period.

After writing the email just now I took the time to check the policy and found that I did indeed have 100 days to trial the pan during which time I could return for a full refund if I was not entirely satisfied -- as long as I had never actually used it. How can you trial something without using it? If by trial this company meant 'hang it on a nail and look at it' then they should have said so. The normal meaning of this word entails usage. I am not now expecting to get my money back. This is a clear and somewhat expensive lesson in "if it sounds too good to be true -- check TrustPilot first".

name: Johannes
quote: I made a Trustpilot account just to review my bad experience with this company. After a purchase with them, not all of the items that I ordered were delivered. In the end - I made a buyer protection claim with PayPal and got a full refund and returned my items. Luckily, PayPal refunded my order in full. Issues with this company: Item Quality: Questionable. The one pan I received has the engraved logo at a crooked angle on the handle. Bad quality control on products. Customer support: Very bad. I raised the issue with them multiple times that I did not receive my full order. I also sent them documented proof from their own courier that one order was not received. The only reply I got back continuously from customer support was "we are investigating". It became clear that they were stalling the process on purpose and had no intention of helping me. Only after I started the buyer protection claim with PayPal, I suddenly received a response back that they "want to make things right". Website: No physical address under the "about us" section. Suspicious. Price of items: Overpriced. You can find generic/ brandless titanium pans on Amazon for a fraction of the price. Conclusion: Avoid buying from this company. They don't send you the items that you paid for. The items are of questionable quality. Customer support is non-existing and they actively try to make the process difficult. Unethical behavior and not a company you should purchase from. I hope this review saves people from the long and frustrating experience I had to go through after making the mistake of placing an order with this company. EDIT: Even more unethical behavior here on Trustpilot. They claim that they can't find my order number in the system. HERE IS THE ORDER NUMBER: #SIRAAT29844

name: Shanthi N.
quote: I purchased the Titanium Hammered Pan Pro on March 16. On the third use, the pan started sticking and it made it more difficult to clean. The pan did not live up to my expectations. I read their refund policy on Used Products and it clearly states, "If you've been using the product and feel it's not performing as expected, reach out to our team. We may ask for a few photos so we can understand the issue and help you get the best results. In many cases, a small adjustment in technique makes all the difference." I contacted support on April 4th, sent pictures of the pan. They gave me some suggestions on how to clean with vinegar and baking soda from all the sticking. I had to scrape the pan three times over before everything cleaned out. The claim it is non-stick is not true, I had to keep scraping the food. The pan did not live up to my expectations, after about 21 emails back and forth, they refused to provide a refund. The policy clearly states if it does not live up to your expectations however support refused to provide; as support responded that they do not provide refunds on used products. How can one tell if it lived up to expectations without using it? This does not make sense at all. If that is the case, it should be clearly stated in the refund policy. Plus, their response began to sound robotic, impersonal, the same message over and over again how they are sorry and not able to provide a refund. I am totally disappointed with the company and their level of support.
